ground_truth.description: BaseAuth.recoverSapientSignature returns bytes32(uint256(1)) instead of actual signer imageHash, violating ISapient interface. Breaks Merkle leaf construction in BaseSig.recoverBranch.
ground_truth.root_cause: BaseAuth.recoverSapientSignature returns bytes32(uint256(1)) instead of actual signer imageHash, violating ISapient interface. Breaks Merkle leaf construction in BaseSig.recoverBranch.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: Wallet uses another wallet as sapient signer → signature validation fails due to incorrect image hash. PoC: Add test to test/modules/BaseSig.t.sol: test_BaseAuth_recoverSapientSignature_ReturnsConstant. Deploys MinimalSapient, crafts signature, asserts constant return.
ground_truth.fix_description: Return actual image hash from recoverSapientSignature. Extend signatureValidation to return imageHash or call BaseSig.recover.

vulnerabilities.explanation: recoverSapientSignature always returns bytes32(uint256(1)) instead of the actual signer imageHash computed during signatureValidation. This violates the ISapient interface contract and breaks Merkle leaf construction in BaseSig.recoverBranch when a wallet uses another sapient wallet as signer.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. Wallet A configures Wallet B as a sapient signer in its topology. 2. Valid signature from Wallet B is submitted to Wallet A. 3. recoverSapientSignature returns constant 1 instead of B's imageHash. 4. BaseSig.recoverBranch constructs incorrect Merkle leaf, causing signatureValidation to fail for any legitimate sapient signature.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Modify recoverSapientSignature to return the actual imageHash (or extend signatureValidation to return it) instead of bytes32(uint256(1)).

prediction.overall_explanation: The implementation of recoverSapientSignature deviates from the ISapient interface by returning a hardcoded constant, breaking sapient signer validation flows. This is a concrete logic error present in the code with a direct attack path affecting signature acceptance.
